17 A rigid cross-shaped structure having four arms PO, SO, QO and RO, each 1.00 m long, is
pivoted at O. Forces act on the ends of the arms and on the midpoints of the arms as shown.
P
30 N
50 N
30 N
70 N
O
R
S
20 N
20 N
70 N
50 N
Q
What is the magnitude of the resultant moment on the structure about O?
A
45 N m
B
90 N m
C
120 N m
D
190 N m

hints: Notice where each force acts: ends of the $1.00\text{ m}$ arms are $1.00\text{ m}$ from O, while midpoints are $0.50\text{ m}$ from O.
Use $\text{moment} = F \times d$ with perpendicular distance, and decide clockwise or anticlockwise for each $20\text{ N}$, $30\text{ N}$, $50\text{ N}$ and $70\text{ N}$ force.
Add all clockwise moments together, add all anticlockwise moments together, then subtract to find the magnitude of the resultant moment in $\text{N m}$.
walkthrough: Identify distances: each arm PO, QO, RO, SO is $1.00\text{ m}$ from O, so every end force acts at $d = 1.00\text{ m}$ and every midpoint force acts at $d = 0.50\text{ m}$.

Take anticlockwise as positive. For the horizontal arm, vertical forces give $r \times F$: R end $+1.00 \times 70 = +70\text{ N m}$, RO midpoint $+0.50 \times 20 = +10\text{ N m}$, SO midpoint $+0.50 \times 30 - 0.50 \times 20 = +5\text{ N m}$, S end $+1.00 \times 70 = +70\text{ N m}$.
Add the horizontal-arm moments: $70 + 10 + 5 + 70 = 155\text{ N m}$ anticlockwise.

For the vertical arm, horizontal forces give $-y \times F_x$: PO midpoint $-(0.50)(+50) + (0.50)(+30) = -10\text{ N m}$, QO midpoint $-(-0.50)(-50) = -25\text{ N m}$, a total of $35\text{ N m}$ clockwise.
Resultant $= 155 - 35 = 120\text{ N m}$. The magnitude is $120\text{ N m}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small. It results from sign errors or cancelling opposite forces at the same midpoint instead of adding their separate $F \times d$ moments.

B.explanation: Too small. It is close to using $1.00\text{ m}$ for end forces but $0$ or wrong distance for the $0.50\text{ m}$ midpoint forces.

C.explanation: The clockwise moments total $35\text{ N m}$ and anticlockwise moments total $155\text{ N m}$, giving a resultant of $120\text{ N m}$ about O.

D.explanation: Too large. It results from adding all $F \times d$ magnitudes without subtracting opposite clockwise and anticlockwise senses, or using $1.00\text{ m}$ for midpoint forces.
